summary.intent: Add a reusable project skill, `ci-incident-investigation`, for both Codex and Claude, implementing a handoff spec for investigating failed CI incidents with evidence preservation, retry assessment, durable test-state repair and issue routing.
summary.outcome: Created SKILL.md (73 lines) and openai.yaml under .agents/skills/ with a symlink in .claude/skills/; validator, lint and Codex discovery pass, and 8 spec scenarios were run with mocked sub-agents (all passed). Nothing was committed.

repo: Canonical project skills live in .agents/skills/<name>/ (Codex), exposed to Claude via a symlink in .claude/skills/; this is the first symlink the repo tracks.
Codex skills need agents/openai.yaml with name and short description; the repo's prettier config requires single quotes in that YAML.
Repo-specific tracker CLI and label conventions live in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md and docs/agents/triage-labels.md; the skill points to them instead of hard-coding.
Repo gate `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` must pass; the worktree has no node_modules, so markdownlint and prettier ran via npx.
Unrelated .husky/_/ folder exists in the worktree and should be excluded from commits.
The skill delegates to `staging-e2e-triage` for failed Staging E2E jobs and to `diagnosing-bugs` only when available.

code.finding: Skill has 8 steps, each with a completion criterion, plus reference sections for retries/evidence, durable test state, privacy and outputs. After scenario 3 a rule was added requiring a check that a second failure keeps its own evidence before a retry.

workflow: Behavior-test skills by giving one Sonnet sub-agent per scenario fixture with mocked CI/tracker/account interfaces and grading the decisions, not wording.
System python3 lacked PyYAML; the skill-creator validator ran via `uv run --with pyyaml`.
`codex exec` from the worktree is a reliable way to confirm which skills Codex discovers; checking binary strings was inconclusive.
Run scenario sub-agents in parallel, but keep full test suites central to avoid RAM starvation.

friction: System python3 lacked PyYAML, so the validator needed a uv workaround.
Worktree had no node_modules, forcing npx for lint tools.
Inspecting the Codex binary for known skill paths was inconclusive and required asking Codex directly.
Scenario 3 exposed a gap in the first draft that required a post-hoc edit.
open_items: Scenarios were not re-run after the rule added following scenario 3.

Skill is uncommitted; proposed branch docs/ci-incident-investigation-skill, commit message `docs: add a CI incident investigation skill`, and a draft PR with no attribution lines, awaiting user approval.
Skill was validated only with mocked interfaces; no live CI or account behavior was tested.
The spec's open follow-up issues (#2394-#2397) and the lack of a clean post-repair nightly remain outside this work.
